title: The Regatta Cup
lesson: Fix the clock, and the story moves.
intro: The Wrenhaven Regatta Cup, solid silver and a hundred years old, has vanished from its cabinet in the Yacht Club boathouse.
The cleaner saw it at half past nine as St Brigid's struck the half. When the steward got back at 22:17, the cabinet was open and the Cup was gone. Picking that lock takes at least four minutes.
Three people had keys, debts or grudges. All three have alibis. In this town, though, half the clocks are wrong.

people.name: Marlow Quint
people.blurb: Club treasurer. Pressed suit, frayed cuffs, a bookie who knows his name.

people.name: Ines Delacroix
people.blurb: Rival skipper from Brittany. Lost the Cup on a protest last year. Hasn't forgotten.

people.name: Rolf Abernethy
people.blurb: Boathouse steward for thirty years. Has the only other key to the cabinet.

clocks.name: The Lantern's bar clock
clocks.note: Sid keeps it slow so last orders come later.

clocks.name: Harbour Café clock & till
clocks.note: Dot sets the till by the wall clock. The wall clock is wrong.

incident.title: The Regatta Cup
incident.text: The Regatta Cup was lifted from its locked cabinet in the boathouse. Seen at 21:30, missing at 22:17. Picking the lock takes 4 minutes.

cards.title: Radio Times
cards.text:
21:00 · THE NEWS
read by Brian Perkins

cards.title: Sid Barrow
cards.text: “We stopped the darts when the nine o'clock news came on the wireless. Our clock said ten to nine. I remember thinking they were early.”
cards.firm: “Ten to nine on our clock, news on the wireless. Clear as day.”

cards.title: Porter's ledger
cards.text:
Miss I. DELACROIX, Room 12
1 × cognac, signed to the room.

cards.title: Sid Barrow
cards.text: “Miss Delacroix came in asking about the morning tide. Twenty past nine by our clock.”
cards.firm: “Twenty past nine. I looked straight at the clock over the bar. Mind you, nobody in here trusts that clock.”

cards.title: Exchange log
cards.text:
Grand Hotel, Room 12 → LYON, FRANCE
Trunk call · 6 minutes

cards.title: Till receipt
cards.text:
Pie & peas, mug of tea
PAID BY CARD · R. ABERNETHY

cards.title: Sid Barrow
cards.text: “Rolf played darts with the lads from twenty past nine by our clock till he left at ten to ten. Said he had his rounds to do.”
cards.firm: “Twenty past to ten to, by the clock. He lost, as usual.”

cards.title: Police desk log
cards.text:
Telephone from R. Abernethy, steward, Yacht Club:
“The Regatta Cup's gone.”

cards.title: Darts slate
cards.text:
M. QUINT · 2 pints · settled
Time chalked off the clock over the bar.

cards.title: Marlow Quint
cards.text: “I walked down from the Lantern and sat in the Harbour Café from twenty to ten until half ten with the evening paper. Ask Dot.”
cards.reply: “So I dawdled. Sue me. But I had a coffee at 21:52, it's on the docket, and I paid for a brandy by card a little after ten. The bank logs every card. The boathouse is ten minutes each way, Detective, and that lock takes picking. Do the arithmetic.”

cards.title: Table docket
cards.text:
Coffee, slice of parkin · CASH
“Mr Quint” in Dot's hand.

cards.title: Dot Pike
cards.text: “Mr Quint came in at quarter to ten by our clock and sat at table four with his paper all evening. His coat never left the chair.”
cards.reply: “His coat was on the chair the whole time… but I was out the back washing up for a good while. He could have slipped out the side door. Oh dear.”

cards.title: Card authorisation
cards.text:
M. QUINT · HARBOUR CAFE
£1.20 · brandy coffee · approved

triggers.question: The Grand's ledger has Ines drinking cognac at 21:20, and Sid has her at the Lantern at 21:20. They're nine minutes' walk apart. Who's wrong, or whose clock is?
Marlow settled his slate at the Lantern at 21:35. The café is seven minutes' walk away, yet he says he sat down at 21:40.
On the corrected café clock, Dot has Marlow sitting down at 21:40. He was still paying at the Lantern at 21:35.

triggers.memo: The Lantern's clock is ten minutes slow. Everything Sid timed by it just moved.
The café clock is five minutes fast, and so is every docket it stamped.

memos.text: Clocks lie too. When two cards describe the same moment, drag one onto the other and hold it there a moment, or click one and choose Same moment as…
Before you call Sid a liar, ask which clock he was reading.
Everyone's covered. Then somebody's cover is false. Look for a moment that's on two clocks.

reconstruction: 21:35. Marlow settles his slate at the Lantern and strolls down the front.
21:47. Coffee and parkin at table four. He leaves his coat and his paper on the chair.
21:57. Out the side door and along the sea wall. Four minutes with a picklock.
22:11. Back at table four. Dot is still at the sink.
22:12. A brandy, paid by card, timed by the bank. That was the alibi.
epilogue: Marlow had been dipping into the club's float for a year to pay his bookie. The Cup was going to be melted down in Polgarth on Monday morning.
It was found in his boot locker, wrapped in a regatta flag. Ines won the race by a length and refused to be gracious about it.
Dot bought the café a new clock. Connie's note: “Remember the Lantern's clock: ten minutes slow. It'll come up again.”
